title: Reader-Respect (Cognitive Restraint) Anti-Patterns
description: 6 anti-patterns the humanizer's Dim 14 (inverse-scored) catches. INVERSE-SCORED dimension: the score measures ABSENCE of these patterns. High score = more cognitive restraint = more respect for the reader's intelligence. Source: arabic-ai-text-humanizer references/14-reader-respect.md.

patterns.title: Tautological affirmation
patterns.description: AI piles synonyms or near-synonyms onto a single concept (مؤكَّد وحقيقي وثابت). Native Arabic prose picks one.

patterns.title: Re-explanation hedges
patterns.description: AI re-states the same point with 'i.e., in other words, that is to say'. Native Arabic prose trusts the reader.

patterns.title: AI-inserted deductive markers
patterns.description: AI announces its conclusion before stating it ('We can deduce from this that...'). Native prose lets the conclusion stand.

patterns.title: Definition of known terms
patterns.description: AI defines terms the reader is presumed to know ('We mean by X that it is...'). Erodes reader trust.

patterns.title: Expectation conformity / surprise suppression
patterns.description: AI announces that something is 'as expected' or 'unsurprising' (كما هو متوقع، بطبيعة الحال). Native prose lets surprise or non-surprise emerge from the content.

patterns.title: Closed / tied-up conclusions
patterns.description: AI ends paragraphs with neat summaries ('In short, we have seen that...'). Native essays let the argument breathe.

scoring_notes: Dim 14 score = 15 - min(15, total_pattern_hits * 2). High score (12-15) = good cognitive restraint. Low score (0-5) = heavy AI fingerprint. Inverse-scored because the dimension measures ABSENCE of patterns, not presence of features.
